english: Sebill arrived at a door marked "Acquisitions." The coachman escorted her to the door and gave it two hard knocks. It opened to reveal a miniscule butcher. The dwarf looked up at the coachman and noted Sebill. "Good! Good!" he said and ushered them into what looked like a carpenter's workshop-only one in which the wood bled when cut. "I commend you on your haste; we here are great appreciators of body magic, you know. You ought to be well paid for your effort. Do you need new horses?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"They are well," answered the coachman, "they're of strong breed and can withstand the spells. With enough food and rest tonight they'll have their stamina back."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"They're fine animals, aren't they?" the dwarf said affably, clearing tools off a table. He was joined by a graying female dwarf wearing an equally dirty apron. "Splendid!" she said. "Let's get started. I'm Odea, he's Hahm, in case he didn't introduce himself."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Anton," said the coachman.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Odea turned to examine Sebill. "Let's get a look at you... Even better than I expected! Let's get you on the table." Anton stepped forward to help lift Sebill, but saw it was unnecessary as Odea, despite her size, moved Sebill to the dwarf-sized table without effort. Odea smiled, "She's empty. No organs. I asked our clients in Nubia to clean her to prevent spoiling. Kept out of the sun the bodies can make the trip in adequate shape." Anton nodded. Odea thought he seemed uneasy. "I'm sorry, did you know her?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No, no... I have no idea who she is, or why she's important to the nobles. She doesn't look like an aristocrat." He paused, then motioned toward the door, "I have the rest of the delivery in my carriage."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Her blood I'm sure. Would you fetch that? Hahm needs to check it and make sure the preservers held up. There are a number of naturally occurring blood thinners in just about every land, but ours are better. I have some theories about speeding the reactions to make the ink less corrosive, but that would require entropy mana which can be hard to come by..."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Outside, Anton gave the blood to Hahm and moved his horses into the shade. This was his first visit to the Luchuirp lands. He admitted to himself that he'd always been a little racist toward dwarves, but couldn't think of any reason why. He looked at and admired the structure of the Catacomb Libralus; from what he'd heard he assumed it was nothing more than a one-trick curiosity shop. It was originally built as a catacomb open to all, until necromancers developed a habit of exploiting it, leading to the pejoration of the name "Free-Use Catacombs." Later it was acquired by a wealthy polymath, who turned it into the institution that is now commonly nicknamed the "Catacomb Librarius." Above ground it was a simple structure with short walls and an entrance adorned with arches and pillars.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Anton returned to the workshop to see Odea in the process of skinning Sebill. Incisions ran up the middle of her chest, along her collarbone, and above her hips. Odea was paring the fatty membrane holding skin to muscle as she pulled the skin upward. Anton groaned at the sight, which alerted Odea that he'd returned. She explained, her enthusiasm outweighing her sympathy for Anton's uneasiness, "The skin's in good shape. We use it all. Her back-because its smoother and thicker-will be tanned and used to make the cover. The rest we stretch into vellum for the pages." Odea paused, Anton was staring at Sebill's body. "It's not pretty, I know. This is an honorable afterlife though. I used to do golemcraft, but animating a golem is like rolling a stone down a hill-it's predictable, it's all it does. Books are the perfect synthesis of form and function, body and spirit, mythos and logos. They are us in every way." She put down her knife, and Anton sat on short ladder. Odea continued, "We can put any talent to use here. Do you practice magic?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I do some, just tricks to help my deliveries-speed the horses, hide my wares. Just dabblings."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Ice! Imagine what you could do with ice mana! We could add people from any corner of Erebus to our collection. You could make your fortune just transporting food to soldiers. Ah, if only we could get some..." Anton laughed. He'd thought of this before. Odea continued, "We use a range of magic here: body helps us transform the person, but that's mostly handiwork; our diviners use spirit magic to contact the dead; and enchanters can infuse the books with special properties. Luckily we're in a land where necromancy is outlawed, or we'd have a lot to worry about. Should I take you to see some of our collection?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Thank you," he replied, "but I have to stable my horses first. I should find an inn."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Fine by me. I need to work and I can't have distractions. Come back later for a tour." Odea smiled, "Now get out of here."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A week had passed since Anton delivered Sebill. He'd gone north to meet a Calabim rendezvous who took the carriage, leaving Anton with a horse. Now returning to the fortified city, he spent the evening at a public house, waiting for nightfall. He made his way back to the Catacomb Libralus and to the door marked "Acquisitions." He knocked. If Odea answered he'd have an excuse for being there. If she didn't, then things would be according to plan. He picked the lock and slipped inside. There was barely any light and he waited for his eyes to adjust. The tables were clean and the tools put away. A door in back opened to a lantern-lit corridor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]When he entered the main hall he realized he'd underestimated the age and grandeur of this place. He thought the library at his former mages' guild was large, but he'd never seen this many books. The hall was lined with shelves of books in every skin color, all facing out. Numerous corridors descended into the catacombs, all filled with books. Anton despaired when he wondered how he would find a single book in all this, until he saw the years inscribed above the corridors' arches.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He entered the most recent corridor, which had just started to be used in the last five years. He walked straight to the end of the row. A small engraving was underneath the last book. Some Malakim name; the book was too dark anyway and had a tattoo of a lion on the cover. The second-to-last book was a pale tan, like a dry meadow. The engraving underneath read "unknown" and named the year of death. The book before that was grayish green and had a single horn jutting out from the spine. He picked up the tan one. It was about two hands tall and a little less wide. The cover was soft-it was leather after all. The spine was sturdy. Bone? He imagined it was her sternum, and thought of her breasts, one skinless, the other just dead. He opened the cover and ran his finger along the inside spine. The pages were sewn to the cover using string made of brown hair. There was writing on the first page, in ink that was still reddish and had not faded into brown. It said: My dear Ain-You'll never read this, but please know that I love you eternally. A chill shook him. He tucked Sebill's book into his pack and returned to the main hall.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He looked at the dates above the arches, and walked down the next corridor. Both sides of the corridor were lined with books facing each other. A jumble of names grew in his head as he scanned the engravings.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Are you looking for something, Anton?" He spun to see Odea in the middle of the corridor. She looked relaxed; he tried his best to appear the same. Her apron was gone and she was dressed comfortably, striking Anton as quite pretty.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Um... yes. A book. A book of... my grandfather."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Anything else?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"...No."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"What was his name?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Anton glanced toward the main hall to see if Odea was alone. "Gerard Cormand."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I know of him! Quite the revolutionary in his day. Did you know him?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I didn't. My father opposed his politics and left the city, taking his family along. I was born on a farm."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Your grandfather was murdered before the revolution ended, wasn't he?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes. I have to know that it wasn't... my father."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Your grandfather is here," she pointed farther down the corridor. Anton cautiously followed her lead. "Our diviners enjoy limited success as a writing tool for the dead, allowing them to make a final statement."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The dead write?" probed Anton.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We ask them if there's anything they'd like to say. They're usually thinking about what they would have done differently in life, so they're full of advice. They might eulogize themselves, or tell their entire life's story-we give the diviners a short vacation to recover after those. These are good souls, mind you; we don't even want to know the dangers of making an unscrupulous book."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"That woman," thought Anton, "what had she done to make her so valuable to the Calabim?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Victims of murder usually have something to say..." Odea stopped walking and motioned toward a book, smaller than Sebill's and paler.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Anton said, "Would he have named his killer?" Odea didn't answer, and Anton lifted his grandfather's book. He opened it and read: I liked the fleshy sins best. He turned the pages: blank. He sighed deeply, and put the book down. Odea took a step back. "Are you going to return the other book too?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Anton faced Odea with a widened stance. "No. I'm sorry, but I'm stealing it." He held a knife at her eye level and took a slow step toward her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I can't stop you," she said calmly. "This is a mistake though. These books are extremely dangerous in the wrong hands. They must never leave."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I know. Your ‘clients' haven't given me any choice though." They circled each other in a cautious dance. Seeing the main hall clear, Anton left through the front door.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Outside the city walls, Anton snuck to his horse, mounted her, and pointed her back north. He hadn't ridden far when a sudden strong wind, or that's what it felt like, threw him off his horse, spilling his pack. He saw in the dark the looming shape of a gargoyle, its wings blocking the light from the city. He ran, and would have died on the spot if it weren't for his haste spell. Instead, he died at the forest's edge a short length away, while the Book of Sebill remained beside the road.

塞比尔来到一扇标着「收货」的门前。车夫领她走到门边，重重地敲了两下。门开了，露出一个身材极其矮小的屠夫。那矮人抬头看了看车夫，又注意到塞比尔。「好！好！」他说着，把他们让进一间看似木匠作坊的屋子——只不过这里的木头被切开时会流血。「你们赶得这么急，值得称赞；要知道，我们这儿可是身体魔法的忠实拥趸。你们该为这番辛劳拿一笔好报酬。要换新马吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「马儿都好，」车夫答道，「它们是良种，扛得住那些法术。今晚只要吃饱睡足，明天体力就能恢复。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「都是好牲口，是不是？」矮人和气地说，一边把桌上的工具收开。一个头发花白、系着同样脏兮兮围裙的女矮人走过来加入他。「太好了！」她说，「咱们开始吧。我叫奥迪亚，他是哈姆——怕他没自我介绍。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「安东，」车夫说。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]奥迪亚转身打量塞比尔。「让我瞧瞧你……比我预想的还要好！来，躺到桌上去。」安东上前想帮忙抬塞比尔，却发现根本用不着——奥迪亚个头虽小，却毫不费力地把塞比尔挪到了矮人尺寸的桌子上。奥迪亚笑道：「她是空的，没有内脏。我托努比亚的客户把她清理干净，免得腐坏。只要不见太阳，尸体旅途中就能保持得像样。」安东点点头。奥迪亚觉得他神情不安。「抱歉，你认识她吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「不，不……我根本不知道她是谁，也不知道她对那些贵族为何重要。她看着不像贵族。」他顿了顿，朝门口示意，「其余的货还在我的马车上。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「是她的血吧，我猜。能去取来吗？哈姆得检查一下，确认防腐剂还管用。几乎每片土地上都有天然的抗凝血物，可我们的更好。我有几套加快反应的理论，能让墨水不那么腐蚀，不过那得用熵之能量，那玩意儿可不好弄……」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]门外，安东把血交给哈姆，把马牵到阴凉处。这是他头一回来到鲁崔尔普人的土地。他向自己承认，他一直对矮人有点偏见，却又想不出任何缘由。他打量着书页地陵的建筑，暗自赞叹；照他所听说的，他本以为这不过是家只会一样把戏的稀奇铺子。这地方最初是座向所有人开放的地陵，直到死灵法师们养成了利用它的恶习，才使「自由地穴」这名声败坏下来。后来它被一位富有的博学之士买下，改造成如今被人俗称为「书页地陵」的机构。地面上不过是座简单的建筑，矮墙环绕，入口以拱门与立柱装点。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]安东回到作坊，看见奥迪亚正在给塞比尔剥皮。切口沿胸口正中、锁骨一线、以及胯部上方划开。奥迪亚一边把皮向上掀起，一边削着连着皮与肌肉的脂肪膜。安东看着这情形呻吟出声，惊动了奥迪亚，让她知道他回来了。她解释道，那份热忱盖过了她对安东不安的体谅：「皮的状态很好，我们全都用得上。她的背——因为更光滑、更厚实——会被鞣制成书封。其余的则拉伸成犊皮纸做书页。」奥迪亚顿了顿，安东正盯着塞比尔的身体。「我知道，这不好看。可这是一种荣耀的来世。我以前做魔像，可给魔像注入生命就像把石头滚下山坡——它是可预料的，它就只会那一件事。而书籍是形式与功能、肉体与精神、神话与理性的完美合一。它们在每一方面都是我们自己。」她放下刀，安东在一架矮梯上坐下。奥迪亚接着说：「在这里，任何才能都能派上用场。你会施魔法吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「会一点，只是些帮送货的小把戏——催马快跑、藏匿货物。都是些皮毛。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「冰！想想看，有了冰之能量你能做什么！我们就能把埃瑞布斯任何角落的人都收进藏品。光是给士兵运送食物你就能发财。啊，只可惜我们弄不到……」安东笑了。这他早想过了。奥迪亚接着说：「我们这儿用到各种魔法：身体魔法帮我们改造遗体，不过那多半是手上功夫；我们的占卜师用精神魔法与死者沟通；附魔师则能给书本注入特殊属性。幸好我们身处一片死灵法术被明令禁止的土地，否则可有得操心了。要不要我带你去看看我们的一些藏品？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「谢谢，」他答道，「可我得先安顿好我的马。我该去找家客栈。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「随你便。我得干活，容不得分心。晚些再回来参观吧。」奥迪亚笑道，「现在，出去吧。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]安东送来塞比尔已过去一周。他北上去与一个卡拉比姆的接头人碰面，对方取走了马车，只给安东留下一匹马。如今回到这座设防的城市，他在一家酒馆消磨了一晚，等待夜幕降临。他摸回书页地陵，来到那扇标着「收货」的门前，敲了敲。若奥迪亚来应门，他便有了到此的借口；若她不来，那事情就按计划进行。他撬开锁，溜了进去。屋里几乎没有光，他等着眼睛适应。桌子擦得干净，工具都已收好。里屋一扇门通往一条点着提灯的走廊。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]当他步入正厅，才意识到自己低估了这地方的年岁与恢弘。他曾以为从前所在的法师公会那间藏书室已经很大，却从没见过这么多书。厅堂两侧排列着一架架书，各种肤色的书脊一律朝外。无数走廊向下通入地陵深处，处处堆满了书。安东想到要在这浩如烟海中找出一本书，不禁绝望，直到他看见各条走廊拱门上方镌刻的年份。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]他走进最近的一条走廊，这里近五年才开始启用。他径直走到那排书的尽头。最后一本书下方有一小行刻字，是个马拉基姆的名字；那本书本就太暗，封面上还刺着一头狮子的纹样。倒数第二本是浅褐色，像一片干枯的草地。下方的刻字写着「无名」，并注明卒年。再往前那本是灰绿色，书脊上突出一只独角。他拿起那本浅褐色的。约莫两掌高，稍窄一些。封面很软——毕竟是皮革。书脊结实。是骨头吗？他想象那是她的胸骨，又想起她的乳房，一只已剥去皮，另一只只是死了。他翻开封面，用手指沿着内侧书脊摸过去。书页是用褐色头发搓成的线缝在封面上的。首页上有字，墨迹仍泛红，尚未褪成褐色。上面写着：亲爱的艾茵——你永远不会读到这些，但请知道，我永远爱你。一阵寒意攫住了他。他把塞比尔的书塞进背包，回到正厅。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]他看了看拱门上方的年份，走进下一条走廊。走廊两侧的书面面相对地排列着。当他扫视那些刻字时，脑中涌起一团纷乱的名字。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你在找什么东西吗，安东？」他猛地转身，看见奥迪亚站在走廊中央。她神色轻松；他尽力装出同样的模样。她脱去了围裙，穿得随意舒适，安东觉得她相当动人。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「呃……是的。一本书。一本……我祖父的书。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「还有别的吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「……没有。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「他叫什么名字？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]安东瞥了一眼正厅，看奥迪亚是否独自一人。「杰拉德·科曼德。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我知道他！在他那个年代可是个了不得的革命家。你认识他吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「不认识。我父亲反对他的政见，带着一家人离开了那座城。我是在农场出生的。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你祖父是在革命结束前被人谋杀的，对吧？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「是的。我得弄清楚，那不是……我父亲干的。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你祖父就在这儿，」她指向走廊更深处。安东谨慎地跟上她。「我们的占卜师作为死者的书写工具，虽只有有限的成效，却能让死者留下最后的遗言。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「死人会写字？」安东试探道。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我们会问他们有没有想说的。他们通常在琢磨这辈子有什么本该做得不同，所以满肚子劝诫。他们或许会为自己写颂词，或许把一生从头讲到尾——碰上这种，我们得给占卜师放个小假才缓得过来。可要记住，这些都是善良的灵魂；我们连造一本心术不正的书会有什么凶险都不愿去知道。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「那个女人，」安东心想，「她做了什么，竟让卡拉比姆人如此看重？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「被谋杀的人通常都有话要说……」奥迪亚停下脚步，朝一本书示意，那书比塞比尔的更小、更苍白。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]安东说：「他会说出凶手的名字吗？」奥迪亚没有回答，安东拿起了祖父的书。他翻开读道：我最爱那些血肉之罪。他翻着书页：一片空白。他深深叹了口气，把书放下。奥迪亚后退一步。「你连另一本书也要还回来吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]安东双脚叉开，面对着奥迪亚。「不。抱歉，可我要偷走它。」他把一把刀举到与她双眼齐平，缓缓朝她逼近一步。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我拦不住你，」她平静地说，「可这是个错误。这些书落到坏人手里极其危险。它们绝不能离开这里。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我知道。可你那些‘客户'没给我留任何选择。」两人小心翼翼地绕着彼此，像跳一支戒备的舞。见正厅已空，安东从正门离去。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]城墙之外，安东潜到马旁，翻身上马，掉头朝北。他还没跑出多远，一阵突如其来的疾风——至少感觉像风——把他掀下马背，背包也散落一地。他在黑暗中看见一头石像怪逼近的身影，它的双翼遮住了城里透来的光。他拔腿就跑，若不是那道疾行法术，他本会当场毙命。可即便如此，他也只是在不远处的林缘倒下气绝，而《塞比尔之书》则留在了路旁。

english: [TAB]Curse those cards! He'd been so close to winning his passage on the earlier ship, when he was dealt the Curse of Arawn-particularly sickening as it had followed a Seven of Towers which surely would have won him the pot. His luck had been horrendous since then, he'd lost most of his winnings on that game, and then spent a lot more drowning his sorrows. He'd then been woken with a pail of water, finding himself press-ganged into service on a galley heading for the unknown lands. After five torturous days of seasickness, Lanun pirates struck, the galley was sunk and here he was now-after being washed ashore-in a Svartalfar courtroom charged with spying.[PARAGRAPH:1]What did he know about these elves? Civil war was it? Something about Seelie and Unseelie Court. Growing up on a farmstead had left him a little vague on world politics. His eyes looked around this strange court-pretty grandiose décor, with a sense of opulence, certainly not the functional style of his Hippus homeland. His eyes fell on a statuette. There was something not quite right about it... ah... yes... the scales, tipped with coins. So... Mammon has a part to play in this courtroom does he? There were still some coins in his hidden pouch. Once he signaled to the bailiff, things began to gather momentum, indeed Mammon had obviously provided a slick fast-tracking system as he found himself ushered away from the courtroom-at the cost of a few coins-to a private room.[PARAGRAPH:1]"It seems you have been a little down on your luck, and would like to... aha... speed the courtroom process up, so to speak?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes, your honor."[PARAGRAPH:1]"...and you can pay the fine of five coins?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Okay... that seems in order. No need for paper work, I think we can come to a satisfactory conclusion here and now: Guilty as charged, you hang tomorrow. In Esus we Trust."[PARAGRAPH:1]"...but ...but the statuette to Mammon?!"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes, a pretty little thing isn't it? ...and worth its weight in gold I must say."[PARAGRAPH:2]-When entering a courtroom, effort should be made to check the patron Angel before constructing your defense.
chinese: [TAB]该死的牌！他本已离赢得早班船的船票只差一步，偏偏抽到了阿劳恩之诅咒——尤其令人作呕的是，这张牌紧跟在一张塔之七之后，那张牌本几乎稳赢下整锅赌注。自那以后他的运气便糟糕透顶，那一局输掉了大半赢来的钱，随后又花了更多去借酒消愁。接着他被人用一桶水泼醒，发现自己已被强征到一艘驶向未知之地的桨帆船上服役。熬过五天折磨人的晕船，拉努恩海盗突袭而来，桨帆船被击沉，如今——被冲上岸后——他站在一间斯瓦塔尔法的法庭上，被控从事间谍活动。[PARAGRAPH:1]他对这些精灵又了解多少？内战是吧？什么光明宫廷与黑暗宫廷的事。在农庄长大让他对天下大事一知半解。他环顾这陌生的法庭——装潢颇为堂皇，透着一股奢靡之气，绝非他希普斯故土那种讲求实用的风格。他的目光落在一尊小雕像上。它有什么地方不太对劲……啊……对了……那天平，秤盘上摞着钱币。这么说……玛门在这间法庭里也有一份戏要唱？他那隐秘的钱袋里还剩几枚钱币。他一朝法警使了眼色，事情便开始加速运转起来，玛门显然备下了一套顺滑的快速通道，因为他发现自己被人引出法庭——代价是几枚钱币——带进了一间密室。[PARAGRAPH:1]「看来你近来手气不太好，想要……啊哈……让庭审的流程加快些，可以这么说？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「是的，法官大人。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「……你付得起五枚钱币的罚金吗？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「付得起。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「好……那看来没问题了。不必走什么文书程序，我想我们此时此地就能得出个圆满的结论：罪名成立，你明日受绞。以艾苏斯之名，我们信守。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「……可……可献给玛门的那尊雕像呢？！」[PARAGRAPH:1]「是啊，是个漂亮的小玩意儿，不是吗？……而且我得说，它可是与自身重量等值的黄金。」[PARAGRAPH:2]——走进法庭时，应当先弄清庇护的天使是谁，再着手构筑你的辩护。

english: [TAB]Gambling houses are full of assorted dice, card and board games. Some even host pits for animal fights or darker pleasures. The Khazad are known to host rat races while Sheaim adepts summon minor creatures to battle against each other.[PARAGRAPH:1]But one thing is similar across all of them, their most popular game, Somnium. Played on cards among the Balseraphs, on tiles by the Elohim and on crude patches of dried leather by the Clan of Embers the game has permeated all layers of Erebus. That's not to say that house rules don't exist, Overlord faithful often offer extra points for Cups cards, followers of Kilmorph often make Tower cards immune to stealing. But regardless of the specific rules the game remains a fascination for kings and peasants and nearly every gambling house hosts a few men praying desperately to avoid death and turn over the 7 of the suit they are missing.
chinese: [TAB]赌场里满是各式各样的骰子、纸牌与棋盘游戏。有些甚至设有斗兽场，或提供更为阴暗的享乐。卡扎德人以举办老鼠赛跑闻名，而塞安的术士则召唤些小型生物令它们相互厮杀。[PARAGRAPH:1]但有一样东西在所有赌场里都大同小异，那就是它们最受欢迎的游戏——梦牌。巴尔塞拉弗人用纸牌玩它，埃洛希姆人用牌砖玩它，余灰部落则在粗糙的干皮片上玩它，这游戏已渗入埃瑞布斯的每一个阶层。这并不是说没有各家规矩：主宰的信徒常给圣杯牌加算额外点数，基尔莫芙的追随者则常让高塔牌免于被窃。但无论具体规矩如何，这游戏始终令君王与农夫同样着迷，几乎每家赌场里都有那么几个人在拼命祈祷，求能躲过死亡，翻出自己独缺的那一门花色的 7。

english: [LINK=UNIT_FAWN]Chapter 1: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=UNIT_SATYR]Chapter 2: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=BUILDING_MONUMENT]Chapter 3: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Chapter 4: Beltane Cycle[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Although it wasn't uncommon for disciples to miss the evening bell during Beltane, and not unheard of to still be missing the next morning, it was out of character for the bookish disciple Wyren. He had been the least interested in the festival and outside of his religious obligations hadn't attended many of the games or displays that crowded the elven capital.[PARAGRAPH:1]Priest Tuathal watched the flowerbed in concern. The flowers that each bloomed during different parts of the day, arrayed in an arc in order as they bloomed. Numbers marked each section and allowed the flowerbed to function as a large living clock as it was easy to tell the time by looking at the flowers that were in bloom. It was nearly noon and Wyren was still missing.[PARAGRAPH:1]A squirrel chattered loudly above the priest, hoping he may have some treats. Tuathal scowled back, unhappy to see the animal expecting to be fed rather than gathering the food from the forest himself. But the squirrel wouldn't give up and followed the priest from tree to tree as he walked into the grove between the three temples.[PARAGRAPH:1]Tuathal quietly prayed for some guidance. He couldn't help but feel that something bad had happened to Wyren even if everything else seemed normal. Unhappy at being ignored the squirrel climbed out on the branch closest to Tuathal and then jumped from there onto the satyr statue at the center of the grove. But instead of landing gracefully on the satyr's broad arm the squirrel passed completely through the statue and landed with a confused thud on the ground.[PARAGRAPH:1]Tuathal stared in surprise at the squirrel and the statue he had just jumped through. Pulling an acorn from his pocket he scooped the squirrel up onto his shoulder and gave him the nut while studying the statue. The squirrel studied it suspiciously as well.[PARAGRAPH:1]Slowly reaching out Tuathal's hand passed effortlessly through the statue; it was only an illusion. The real statue was gone.[PARAGRAPH:2]Hemah watched as the grove filled up with priests, city watch, and mages investigating the missing statue. He wasn't worried about being noticed, as a significant crowd of curious travelers, disciples and adepts had turned up to watch what was going on.[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon, an elven man with golden hair and green eyes was leading the investigation. He wore the garb of a watch captain but it was obvious from his bearing that he was nobility as well. The captain checked out the statue himself and then after conferring with a shrugging group of mages ordered someone to get Thessa. Hemah leaned forward in interest, this was the first time he had heard her name but he suspected he already knew who she was.[PARAGRAPH:1]While he waited the captain investigated the rest of the grove, ordering people back. He found wagon tracks leading into the grove, and the heavier set leading out. They lead back out to one of the busiest roads in Evermore, where they were impossible to track. But he sent a group of soldiers down the road anyway to see what they could find. He asked another to start questioning the local wagoneers to see if anyone had stored or purchased a wagon capable of carrying a marble statue in the past few days. The day after Beltane there were hundreds of wagons in Evermore that fit that description, but the lieutenant accepted his charge and set off to perform it.[PARAGRAPH:1]Shortly afterwards a beautiful archmage entered the grove and the theorizing mages grew quiet. She talked quietly with the captain, asked a few questions to the mages, who shrugged again, and then went over and knelt down by the statue.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Is the statue of anyone in particular?" she asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]Priest Tuathal scowled but controlled himself before responding, "Surely your studies keep you too long from the temple lady Thessa. The statue is of Gower, favored son of Cernunnos, who was killed by Agares during the first Age. This statue was erected by the elves of that age in memory of him. It is one of the oldest relics in Evermore."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Thieves usually aren't that interested in history and there are a thousand statues in Evermore that would have been easier to steal. Is there any reason why this one would be more valuable?"[PARAGRAPH:1]The priest cleared his throat. The eyes of everyone in the grove went to him and the squirrel on his shoulder glared back at everyone.[PARAGRAPH:1]After an awkward silence Tuathal said, "we may need to talk about that in private."[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon ordered one of his guards to have the priest taken into the temple for a more private conversation. But Thessa ignored the response, to her it was just another example of how the traditions of the Ljosalfar were keeping it from moving ahead. Taking a deep breath she closed her eyes and began to cast.[PARAGRAPH:1]If she was beautiful, she was even more beautiful while in the throes of magic. Her dark hair, unusual among the Ljosalfar, fluttered and her body strained as she channeled the power needed to cast the spell. Hemah recognized it, she would be trying to follow the link between the illusion and the one maintaining it. She was trying to find him. But just before her spell was completed Hemah released the illusion and the statue disappeared.[PARAGRAPH:1]"What happened, did you dispel it?" Devon asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]With the object of her spell gone Thessa struggled to release the magic harmlessly. Her hands glowed as if stars danced from them and then faded out.[PARAGRAPH:1]"No," Thessa answered, "I hadn't done anything yet. The caster released the spell before I could follow it back to him."[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon looked up at the assembled group of spectators, who dumbly returned his gaze. He turned to the last of his lieutenants.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Have everyone here be brought to the barracks for questioning."[PARAGRAPH:1]A few hours later Hemah was still sitting in the barracks waiting to be questioned. All of the citizens of Evermore had been first, and questioning them went relatively quickly. But they were taking their time with the travelers. Hemah had already released the spell he cast on Alazkan's amulet, he hoped it hid him for long enough. And unlike most mages he didn't keep anything magical on him. He was less concerned with the questioning then he was in making sure he got the right questioner.[PARAGRAPH:1]Fortunately Thessa was in charge of examining all the travelers and just after nightfall his name was called and he was shuffled into a small office with her. Thessa looked over the notes a soldier had collected on the group and the items they had taken from Hemah.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Are these yours?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes," Hemah answered.[PARAGRAPH:1]"What are you doing in Evermore?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"I came for the festival." Hemah said somewhat honestly.[PARAGRAPH:1]"A common answer today, do you worship Cernunnos?" Thessa asked the questions as a matter of protocol, she was more interested in looking through the items he had. She had the golden feather, mask and bag of incense laid out on the table and she was carefully examining the feather.[PARAGRAPH:1]"No, I'm not really religious. Though I do enjoy the sights of Evermore and the festival."[PARAGRAPH:1]This was the first time Thessa looked up at him, most of the people she talked to today claimed to be worshipers even if they weren't. He had a gentle face, almost soft and would be handsome if he didn't look so tired. He didn't match what she would expect from a merchant, mage or one of the many people that flocked to Evermore for the festival.[PARAGRAPH:1]"What of these items?" she asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]"The mask is for the festival," Hemah lied, he wore the mask to keep him from seeing his own reflection. That helped keep him from dreaming about himself, which was an exhilarating and terrifying experience.[PARAGRAPH:1]"The feather I found on the edges of your empire. I've only had it for a few days and I'm not sure what to make of it."[PARAGRAPH:1]"It is beautiful." Thessa was more practical than most of the Ljosalfar, and had never seen much value in spiritual or artistic matters but she couldn't deny the draw of the feather. She tested it several times before Hemah came into the room and it was the reason she wanted to question him directly. It wasn't magical, but she couldn't believe the draw it had without magical means.[PARAGRAPH:1]"It's the second most beautiful thing I've seen in your lands."[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah's meaning was obvious from the way he was looking at her, but Thessa pretended to miss the compliment.[PARAGRAPH:1]"And the incense?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"It helps me sleep." Hemah honestly responded, "I have troubling dreams sometimes, but if I burn the incense in the room with me I don't have them."[PARAGRAPH:1]"This is an ancient elven craft, I'm surprised to see anyone with it, especially a human. Did you buy it from someone at the festival?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"No, I met a merchant in Kingsport with it. But I don't know how he got it."[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah paused before continuing.[PARAGRAPH:1]"About the feather... I'd like you to have it."[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa looked surprised and suspicious so Hemah continued.[PARAGRAPH:1]"As I said, I found it at the edge of your empire, so if anything it is yours anyway. It is too beautiful to be stuffed into my tunic for months on end."[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa would never accept a gift from someone being investigated. The fact that he was offering a gift implied his guilt. But she couldn't help feeling that this was different, that this man was lonely and out of place, but not responsible for the disappearance of the statue or disciple Wyren. And she found herself unable to turn down the feather.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Are you sure? This won't affect the investigation at all. You will still likely spend the night in jail."[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah nodded, "I'm sure."[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa tucked the feather in her dark hair and smiled at him. That vision was forever burned into Hemah's heart and it was all he could do to keep from professing his eternal love for her. Then she leaned across, kissed him gently on the cheek, whispered her thanks and left the room. He was left stunned.[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon was watching the interview. There were only a handful of suspects that seemed out of place. Though he suspected they were all dead ends. But seeing Thessa kiss the pale human caused a turmoil of emotions that he was unable to understand.[PARAGRAPH:1]When she came out of the room they met to discuss the results of the interviews. Thessa didn't know he had seen the kiss but sensed immediately that he was distant. As they went through each of the suspects they easily agreed to hold or release each of them until they came to Hemah.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Do you think he is a mage without magic, a kidnapper without a victim, an attacker without a weapon and a thief without the goods? We found the wagoneer that sold the missing wagon, the man he described doesn't match any of our suspects. What is it you suspect about this one?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon was unaccustomed to being so directly questioned from anyone except Thessa, it was one of the things that he loved about her. She was right, but even without the kiss there was something about Hemah that bothered him. Devon's father was an angel in Sucellus's charge and that divine birthright usually made his instincts correct.[PARAGRAPH:1]Unable to settle the dispute they asked priest Tuathal's opinion. He peeked into the room where Hemah sat quietly and considered him. After a few minutes he simply said, "I agree with Devon, there is something suspicious about the man that warrants more scrutiny. I would have him held until we find out more."[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon gave the order before Thessa could object. Then Tuathal stepped in to cool the stubborn archmage's temper.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I heard that Devon proposed to you at the festival dance last night. I am sorry it took me so long to congratulate your betrothal."[PARAGRAPH:1]Tuathal's tactic worked and Thessa let her argument go in the face of the priest's good wishes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes, it was an amazing night. I couldn't be happier."[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon was also relaxed by the memories of the previous night, "Now we have only to set a day."[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa smiled, Hemah's plight was forgotten.[PARAGRAPH:1]A few minutes later guards came and told Hemah he was to be held for further questioning. They led him to a cell where he was locked up with a few pickpockets and a handful of others that were suspected of having something to do with the theft. He went peacefully to the cell, and only argued that he needed his incense so he could sleep. They refused to give it to him and ignored his requests.[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah stayed up for most of the night but as the hours went by he found himself drifting off in short bursts. The sleep from the incense wasn't that restful so it had been weeks since he had really slept. In his short bursts of dreams he saw visions of Thessa, the satyr statue, the golden feather as part of the wings of an ancient god, and that god's attack on this very forest. Visions of withered trees and disease.[PARAGRAPH:1]He shook himself awake. These dreams were horrible but he was so tired that he was falling asleep even as he paced back and forth. Eventually the dreams won.[PARAGRAPH:1]When he awoke the barracks was full of concerned guards, mages and priests. Devon was organizing the efforts and getting reports from scouts checking in from various edges of the forest. After a few hours the guards remembered the travelers they had detained and, seeing no opportunity to pursue the investigation and little hope of finding anything if they did, opened the cell and let them go.[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah had his mask, incense and other items returned and he was released onto the streets of Evermore. Devon excused himself from his meeting and caught up with Hemah as he walked away from the barracks.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You, where are you going?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah couldn't believe he was going to go through this again.[PARAGRAPH:1]"The guards released me, they said the investigation was suspended."[PARAGRAPH:1]"I know," Devon responded. "I mean you will be leaving Evermore. You will be leaving our forest. You won't return."[PARAGRAPH:1]The captain looked angry and Hemah noticed that the other suspects that had been released weren't given the same speech.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I was hoping to talk to the woman who questioned me before I left. Do you know where she is?"[PARAGRAPH:1]The captain's eyes narrowed, Hemah had found the point of the captain's anger at him and immediately regretted asking the question.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Her name is Thessa, and she is betrothed to me. You will not talk to her."[PARAGRAPH:1]At that Devon called a guard over and ordered him to escort Hemah to the edge of the forest. The guard agreed and with a final glare from Devon Hemah was led away from the barracks.[PARAGRAPH:1]As Hemah walked beside the guard he put on his mask. He was an amazing caster and could cast minor spells simply from sheer strength of will. Especially after the prior night's sleep, he felt more rested than he had in months. As he walked he reached out to the guard's mind. He would travel out to the forests edge alone, all the while believing Hemah walked beside him and left without any problems.[PARAGRAPH:1]After the spell was firmly in place Hemah cut down an alleyway and headed to the mage guild of the city, where he guessed Thessa would be searching for a cause of the corruption that occurred last night.[PARAGRAPH:1]There were three ways to become invisible. Bend light around your body, create an illusion on your body of the surface behind it or simply trick the mind of the person looking at you so that they don't think they see you. It was this last form that Hemah used as he walked into the mage guild. He scanned ahead, finding elves and blocking their mind to his presence. Technically everyone he walked by saw him as he wandered through the hallways and studies of the guild, but they didn't realize it.[PARAGRAPH:1]He didn't try to include Thessa in the spell. She was looking through piles of ancient tomes when he entered the room. She still had the golden feather in her hair.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Thessa."[PARAGRAPH:1]She didn't recognize the voice and it took her a second to match the mask with the one she examined the day before. He had a commanding presence and she could feel the magic radiating from him. This figure was much different than the lonely young man she interviewed and a quick touch of her ring warned Devon that she was in danger.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Hemah? What are you doing here?"[PARAGRAPH:1]She reached out and felt the magic flowing through the room, mentally preparing to defend herself against a mental or physical assault. Without thinking she pushed the tomes aside to keep them from getting damaged.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I came for you, this blight consumes hope. It will destroy you or Evermore. You must get out of here."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Did you create it?" What she had seen of the corruption growing in the forest was beyond anything she had seen before. She sensed a lot of power in Hemah, but the corruption was something greater.[PARAGRAPH:1]"No," Hemah replied. "You did. It's a memory of an affliction that struck the forest long ago. It was eventually stopped by an angel, but no such angel exists to stop it now. Come with me."[PARAGRAPH:1]"How do you know about the source of the corruption?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah could feel her gathering power. She was planning to attack him but she wanted to see what she could learn from him first.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Thessa, I don't know the answer to that, things are revealed to me in dreams. Like I know that if you come with me we will be safe."[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon burst through the study door with sword in hand, followed by mages loudly claiming there was nothing threatening the guild. Devon raced across the room, yelling for Thessa to get back but she didn't listen. Instead she channeled a pulse of arcane energy into the room to disrupt any defensive spells Hemah may have active. The mages stopped in alarm as Hemah's invisibility spell dropped and the masked figure popped into view.[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon ducked under Hemah's arm and sliced up along his ribs. Hemah screamed in pain and visions of a sleeping god danced briefly in front of his eyes, in a distant place that god stirred. Thessa prepared another spell as Hemah fell to the floor.[PARAGRAPH:1]Looking up Hemah only said, "Forget," and the impact of the word on the room was dramatic and sudden. It was as if Hemah had never been there.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Why did you set off your ring?" Devon asked in exasperation.[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa stood confused, the mages behind Devon continued their objections to his rush into the guild and their claims that there wasn't any danger here.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I don't know," she answered, "I'm sorry it was an accident."[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon took a deep breath and sheathed his sword. After a few minutes of apologizing to the mages they finally left him alone with Thessa. She pulled a golden feather out of her hair and stared at it in confusion.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Are you okay?" Devon asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]He sat down and wrapped his arms around her, kissing her lightly on the cheek. She relaxed in his arms.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Did you find anything?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"No," Thessa answered, "not yet."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Have you decided on a day for our wedding yet?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa smiled, she wasn't accustomed to pushing off decisions. But she hadn't been able to pick a day yet.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Soon, I promise."[PARAGRAPH:1]Hemah watched Thessa and Devon leave the mage guild late that night. Devon held her as they walked and despite the corruption approaching the city they were enjoying the time they had together. 他转向最后一名副手。[PARAGRAPH:1]「把这里所有人都带到兵营去问话。」[PARAGRAPH:1]几个钟头后，赫玛仍坐在兵营里等着受审。永恒之地的居民都先受了盘问，问他们进行得相对很快。可对那些旅人，他们却慢条斯理。赫玛早已解除了施在阿拉兹干护身符上的法术，他但愿那法术已把他掩藏得够久。而且不同于大多数法师，他身上不带任何带魔法的物件。比起受审，他更在意的是确保自己碰上对的那个审问者。[PARAGRAPH:1]幸而负责审查所有旅人的正是塞莎，入夜不久便叫到他的名字，他被带进一间与她独处的小办公室。塞莎翻看着一名士兵采集的众人记录，以及他们从赫玛身上取走的物件。[PARAGRAPH:1]「这些是你的吗？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「是的，」赫玛答道。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你来永恒之地做什么？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「我为庆典而来。」赫玛答得多少有几分实话。[PARAGRAPH:1]「这是今天常见的回答，你信奉科尔诺诺斯吗？」塞莎照例发问，可她更感兴趣的是翻检他那些物件。她把金色羽毛、面具与一袋熏香摊在桌上，正仔细端详那根羽毛。[PARAGRAPH:1]「不，我算不上信教。不过我确实喜爱永恒之地的风光和这场庆典。」[PARAGRAPH:1]这是塞莎头一回抬眼看他，今天她盘问的人里，大多明明不信却都自称是信徒。他有一张温和的脸，近乎柔弱，若不是显得那样疲惫，本该算得上英俊。他不像她料想中的商人、法师，也不像那许多为庆典涌向永恒之地的人。[PARAGRAPH:1]「这些东西又是怎么回事？」她问。[PARAGRAPH:1]「面具是为庆典准备的，」赫玛撒了谎，他戴面具是为了不看见自己的倒影。那能帮他不再梦见自己——那是一种既令人亢奋又令人惊惧的体验。[PARAGRAPH:1]「那根羽毛我是在你们帝国边境捡到的。我才拿了没几天，还不知该拿它作何解。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「它很美。」塞莎比大多数勒约沙尔法人都更务实，向来看不出灵性或艺术之事有多少价值，可她无法否认这羽毛的吸引力。在赫玛进屋之前，她已试探过它好几回，这也正是她想亲自审问他的缘由。它并无魔力，可她无法相信这般吸引力竟没有魔法的作用。[PARAGRAPH:1]「它是我在你们这片土地上见过的第二美的东西。」[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛的用意从他望着她的眼神里一望便知，可塞莎佯装没听懂这句恭维。[PARAGRAPH:1]「那熏香呢？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「它助我入睡。」赫玛老实作答，「我有时会做些扰人的梦，可只要在屋里点上这熏香，就不会做了。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「这是一门古老的精灵手艺，能见到有人持有它我很意外，何况还是个人类。你是在庆典上从谁那儿买来的吗？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「不是，我是在王港遇到一个带着它的商人。可我不知道他是怎么弄到的。」[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛顿了顿，才接着说下去。[PARAGRAPH:1]「关于那根羽毛……我想把它送给你。」[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎显得既惊讶又生疑，赫玛于是接着说。[PARAGRAPH:1]「我说过，我是在你们帝国边境捡到它的，所以真要论起来，它本就该是你们的。让它塞在我衣襟里一连数月，实在太美了些。」[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎绝不会接受一个受调查者的馈赠。他献上礼物这一举动本身就暗示了他的心虚。可她忍不住觉得这一回有所不同，觉得这男人孤独、格格不入，却与雕像和门徒怀伦的失踪无关。而她发现自己竟无法拒绝那根羽毛。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你确定吗？这丝毫不会影响调查。你多半今晚仍得在牢里过夜。」[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛点点头，「我确定。」[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎把羽毛插进自己深色的发间，朝他微微一笑。那一幕永远烙进了赫玛心里，他费尽全力才没有当场倾吐对她永恒的爱意。随后她探身过来，在他脸颊上轻轻一吻，低声道谢，走出了房间。他呆立当场。[PARAGRAPH:1]德文一直在旁观这场审问。看着确实出格的嫌疑人只有寥寥数个。虽说他怀疑这些人到头来都会是死胡同。可眼看塞莎亲吻那苍白的人类，一股他自己也理不清的情绪翻涌上来。[PARAGRAPH:1]她走出房间后，两人碰头商议审问的结果。塞莎不知他看见了那一吻，却立刻察觉他神情疏远。他们逐一过着嫌疑人，轻易就商定了各人是扣是放，直到轮到赫玛。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你当真觉得他是个没有魔法的法师、没有受害者的绑匪、没有凶器的袭击者、没有赃物的窃贼？我们找到了卖出那辆失踪马车的车夫，他描述的那人跟我们任何一个嫌疑人都对不上号。你到底怀疑这一个什么？」[PARAGRAPH:1]德文不习惯被人如此直截了当地质问，除了塞莎——而这正是他爱她的地方之一。她说得没错，可即便撇开那一吻，赫玛身上也有某种东西让他心神不宁。德文的父亲是一位受苏切鲁斯差遣的天使，那神圣的血脉往往让他的直觉不会出错。[PARAGRAPH:1]二人争执不下，便去征询图阿萨尔祭司的意见。他往赫玛静坐的房间里探了探，端详着他。过了几分钟，他只淡淡说道：「我同意德文，这人身上有些可疑之处，值得再加盘查。我会先把他扣下，等我们查明更多再说。」[PARAGRAPH:1]不等塞莎反对，德文便下了令。随后图阿萨尔上前，安抚这位倔强大魔法师的火气。[PARAGRAPH:1]「我听说德文昨晚在庆典舞会上向你求了婚。我这么晚才来道贺你们的婚约，真是抱歉。」[PARAGRAPH:1]图阿萨尔这一招奏了效，面对祭司的美好祝愿，塞莎放下了争执。[PARAGRAPH:1]「是的，那是个美妙的夜晚。我再幸福不过了。」[PARAGRAPH:1]德文也因昨夜的回忆而神情舒缓，「如今我们只剩挑个日子了。」[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎莞尔一笑，赫玛的困境被抛到了脑后。[PARAGRAPH:1]几分钟后，守卫前来告诉赫玛，他将被扣下以待进一步问话。他们把他带到一间牢房，与几个扒手和另几个被疑与这桩窃案有牵连的人一同关押。他平静地走进牢房，只争辩说自己需要熏香才能入睡。他们不肯给他，对他的请求置之不理。[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛大半夜都醒着，可随着时辰流逝，他发觉自己一阵阵短促地睡去。熏香带来的睡眠并不那么安稳，因此他已有好几周不曾真正睡过。在这一阵阵短促的梦中，他看见了塞莎、萨提尔雕像、化作某位远古之神翅膀一部分的金色羽毛，以及那位神对这片森林的攻击。种种枯木与瘟疫的幻象。[PARAGRAPH:1]他猛地惊醒。这些梦骇人至极，可他实在太累，连来回踱步时也在睡去。终究，睡梦占了上风。[PARAGRAPH:1]当他醒来，兵营里满是忧心忡忡的守卫、法师与祭司。德文正在调度各方，接收着从森林各处边缘归来的斥候的报告。几个钟头后，守卫想起了他们扣押的那些旅人，眼见既没有机会继续调查，就算查下去也几乎无望有所斩获，便打开牢房，把他们放了。[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛领回了他的面具、熏香和其余物件，被放到永恒之地的街上。德文从会议上抽身，赶上正从兵营走开的赫玛。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你，你要去哪儿？」[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛简直不敢相信自己又要把这一套重来一遍。[PARAGRAPH:1]「守卫放我走了，他们说调查中止了。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「我知道，」德文答道，「我的意思是，你将离开永恒之地。你将离开我们的森林。你不许再回来。」[PARAGRAPH:1]队长面带怒色，赫玛注意到，其他被释放的嫌疑人可没得到同样一番训话。[PARAGRAPH:1]「我本想在走之前跟盘问我的那位女士谈谈。你知道她在哪儿吗？」[PARAGRAPH:1]队长眯起双眼，赫玛这才找到队长对他动怒的症结所在，立刻懊悔提了这个问题。[PARAGRAPH:1]「她叫塞莎，她是我的未婚妻。你不许跟她说话。」[PARAGRAPH:1]说罢德文唤来一名守卫，命他把赫玛押送到森林边缘。守卫应了，在德文最后一记瞪视下，赫玛被带离了兵营。[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛走在守卫身旁，戴上了自己的面具。他是个了不起的施法者，单凭意志之力便能施展些小型法术。尤其在前一夜的睡眠之后，他觉得自己比数月来任何时候都更为神清气爽。一路走着，他探入守卫的心神。守卫会独自走到森林边缘，一路都笃信赫玛就走在他身旁，随后毫无异样地离去。[PARAGRAPH:1]待法术稳稳生效，赫玛拐进一条小巷，直奔城中的法师公会——他猜塞莎会在那里追查昨夜那场腐化的根源。[PARAGRAPH:1]隐形有三种法子。让光绕过你的身体，在你身上造出身后表面的幻象，或者干脆蒙骗观看者的心神，让他们以为自己没看见你。赫玛走进法师公会时用的正是最后这种。他向前扫视，找到那些精灵，封住他们的心神使之察觉不到他的存在。严格说来，他穿过公会的廊道与书房时，途经的每个人都看见了他，只是他们没有意识到罢了。[PARAGRAPH:1]他没打算把塞莎也纳入法术。他进屋时，她正翻检着一堆堆古老的典籍。她发间仍插着那根金色羽毛。[PARAGRAPH:1]「塞莎。」[PARAGRAPH:1]她没听出这声音，过了一秒才把面具与前一天她端详过的那副对上号。他有一种令人臣服的气场，她能感到魔力从他身上散发出来。这身影与她盘问过的那个孤独青年判若两人，她指尖一触戒指，便向德文示警她身陷险境。[PARAGRAPH:1]「赫玛？你来这儿做什么？」[PARAGRAPH:1]她探出感知，觉察到魔力在屋里流动，暗自准备抵御精神或肉体的攻击。她不假思索地把那些典籍推到一旁，免得它们受损。[PARAGRAPH:1]「我为你而来，这场枯萎正吞噬着希望。它会毁掉你，或毁掉永恒之地。你必须离开这里。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「是你造出它的？」她所见到的那在森林中滋长的腐化，超乎她从前见过的任何事物。她感到赫玛身上蕴着极大的力量，可那腐化却是更甚一筹的存在。[PARAGRAPH:1]「不是，」赫玛答道，「是你。它是很久以前袭击这片森林的一场灾厄的记忆。那灾厄最终被一位天使所止，可如今再没有这样一位天使能止住它。跟我走。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「你怎么会知道这腐化的根源？」[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛能感到她正在积蓄力量。她打算攻击他，可她想先看看能从他口中探出些什么。[PARAGRAPH:1]「塞莎，这个问题我答不上来，种种事情是在梦里向我揭示的。就像我知道，只要你跟我走，我们就能平安无事。」[PARAGRAPH:1]德文手持长剑破门而入，身后跟着几名法师，大声嚷嚷说没有什么在威胁公会。德文疾奔过屋子，喊塞莎退后，可她不听。相反，她把一道奥术能量的脉冲注入房间，以扰乱赫玛可能正维持着的任何防护法术。赫玛的隐形法术随之破解，那戴面具的身影蓦地现出，法师们惊愕地僵住了。[PARAGRAPH:1]德文从赫玛臂下一低身，顺着他的肋骨向上一划。赫玛痛叫出声，一位沉睡之神的幻象在他眼前一闪而过——在某个遥远之地，那位神动了动。塞莎在赫玛倒地之际备下了另一道法术。[PARAGRAPH:1]赫玛抬起头，只说了一个字：「忘记，」这个字在房间里激起的冲击既剧烈又突然。就仿佛赫玛从不曾到过这里。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你为什么触发你的戒指？」德文懊恼地问。[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎茫然站着，德文身后的法师们仍在抗议他闯进公会，坚称这里根本没有任何危险。[PARAGRAPH:1]「我不知道，」她答道，「对不起，是个意外。」[PARAGRAPH:1]德文深吸一口气，把剑插回鞘中。向法师们赔了几分钟不是后，他们终于让他与塞莎独处。她从发间抽出一根金色羽毛，困惑地盯着它。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你没事吧？」德文问。[PARAGRAPH:1]他坐下，双臂环住她，在她脸颊上轻轻一吻。她在他怀里松弛下来。[PARAGRAPH:1]「你查到什么了吗？」[PARAGRAPH:1]「没有，」塞莎答道，「还没有。」[PARAGRAPH:1]「你决定好我们的婚期了吗？」[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎微微一笑，她不习惯拖延决定。可她始终没能挑出一个日子。[PARAGRAPH:1]「快了，我保证。」[PARAGRAPH:1]那天深夜，赫玛望着塞莎与德文离开法师公会。德文一路搂着她走，尽管腐化正逼近这座城，他们仍享受着相守的时光。赫玛把熏香倒在街上，他再也不惧怕那些梦了。[PARAGRAPH:1][NEWLINE][NEWLINE][LINK=LEADER_THESSA]第五章：五月节轮回[\\LINK]

english: [TAB]In most Luchuirp cities, the sculptor's studio can be found next to the graveyard. Charged with crafting both golems and gravestones, the mason's art perfectly embodies both life and death.[PARAGRAPH:1]It is a well-known fact that the craft of a sculptor is often one of the most profitable professions within Luchuirp society. Many years ago, a young sculptor carved an iron golem with the face of Athos Ulthane, the savior of Ironstone Pass. Since that day many prominent citizens became supporters of the arts in the hope that they might be remembered in a similar fashion.[PARAGRAPH:1]Yet what of the lesser golems, those baked from mud and clay and the detritus of the streets. The silent servants that perform the tasks that no one else wants to. Who knows what faces adorn these pitiless creatures? Ask all you want. For all the words written in the heads, none will ever emerge from their lips.[PARAGRAPH:1]But if you pay for sufficient drinks and listen carefully to the whispers of the right rotgut beggar in the wrong part of Ithralia, you might learn that the golem which cleans the sewers at the docks bears an uncanny resemblance to Hamish Two-Strings, the infamous murderer and thief.[PARAGRAPH:1]In death, as in life, social hierarchies remain, carved in metal and stone and clay forever.
chinese: [TAB]在大多数鲁崔尔普城市里，雕塑师的工坊都紧挨着墓地。既要打造魔像，又要凿刻墓碑，石匠的技艺将生与死完美地融于一体。[PARAGRAPH:1]众所周知，雕塑师的手艺往往是鲁崔尔普社会中最赚钱的行当之一。许多年前，一位年轻的雕塑师雕出了一尊铁魔像，面容取自铁石关的救主阿特斯·乌鲁珊。自那天起，许多显要市民便成了艺术的资助者，指望自己也能以同样的方式被人铭记。[PARAGRAPH:1]可那些更卑微的魔像又如何呢——那些由泥土、黏土和街头污物烧制而成的。那些默默无声、去做旁人都不愿做之事的仆役。谁又晓得这些无情造物顶着什么样的面孔？你尽管去问吧。纵然那一颗颗头颅里写满了字句，却没有一个字会从它们唇间吐出。[PARAGRAPH:1]但你若肯掏钱买足够多的酒，又肯在伊斯拉利亚不该去的地界仔细听那对的一个烂醉乞丐的窃语，或许就能得知：那清理码头下水道的魔像，与臭名昭著的杀人越货之徒、「双弦」哈米什长得出奇地像。[PARAGRAPH:1]死后一如生前，社会的等级依旧长存，被永远地雕刻在金属、石头与黏土之中。

english: In the frozen tundra of the Age of Ice people rarely had to worry about preserving their meat for the future, for the incredibly low temperatures could keep most foodstuffs in stasis for an indefinite period. In the rare cases where hunters caught more meat than they could carry on their backs, they usually dug a hole a few feet deep and deposited it there, where the cold kept it fresh and several heavy boulders prevented scavengers. Once they lost this natural refrigeration in the Age of Rebirth though, they had to relearn how to properly treat meat against rot, generally by drying and smoking it as it hung from the rafters of a special smokehouse.
chinese: 在冰之纪元那冰封的苔原上，人们鲜少需要为将来储存肉食而操心，因为那极端的低温能让大多数食物无限期地保持不腐。偶有猎人捕到多得背不动的肉，他们通常会挖一个几尺深的坑把肉存进去，那里的严寒使其保鲜，几块沉重的巨石则挡住食腐动物。可到了重生之纪元，他们失去了这份天然的冷藏，便不得不重新学习如何妥善处理肉食以防腐坏——通常是把肉挂在一间特制熏制房的椽子上，将其风干并烟熏。

english: As the sun set into the ocean, its colors multiplied and shone across the sedated waters. Dying light in grapefruit and blood-orange shades pierced the temple's windows and comingled with the blues and greens, never mixing. The lights shimmered across the town's rooftops, glowing like the tolling of church bells as worshippers walked to the ocean and temple. For some, worship was to admire the ocean, to be present at its show. Others preferred immersion, giving their bodies to the water (metaphorically) as a way of saying "I owe you everything." Inside the temple the faithful bathed in the flowing water, letting the incense riding in the thick air penetrate their skin. Their minds flowed with the water and gave way to visions and serenity. A Priest of Whispers watched over as the din of the chamber filled with echoes of mumblings, humming, and short cries of ecstasy.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Farther within the temple, Captain Grey-Eye of the Jury Rig raised his head after bowing to High Speaker The Bones of Its Mother Are Luminous Eyes.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"What have you brought us, Captain?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Grey-Eye was as faithful to the priests as any successful sea captain should be. He prayed regularly, both on the waves and on shore, and always gave a portion of his gold spoils back to the sea. Such spoils were what brought him before the Speaker in his hometown temple.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Rumors from the Calabim lands speak of rich bounties for a treasure they've apparently misplaced."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I know. The ebb and flow of water brings me news from around the world."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Then y'know better than I the significance of the Book of Sable; I know none more than what they've offered to pay."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Speaker stared through unblinking, sunken eyes. He was hairless, pale, and skeletal but his voice was like the creaking of the Jury Rig's mast. He was Speaker when Grey-Eye worshipped here as a child and hadn't changed appearance.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I will pay anything you ask. However, when the bargaining is done I have a favor to ask of you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You're too generous, Your Resonance. If you're paying in Lanun coins, I'll take the Calabim's price. I accept the favor-what is it?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I'm sending a priestess with you on your ship. She has a mission and you will find her abilities useful. Leave the book on the altar. Your service has been invaluable as always, Captain." Grey-Eye bowed his head and was escorted away. The Speaker regarded the book in front of him. The cover was a lightly colored and flimsy leather, dirty and weathered. The pages were becoming brittle. Human flesh no doubt; a product of the Catacomb Libralus, whose books were well guarded by the golems. No books ever left that city, making the Book of Sable especially rare. The High Speaker knew it was not chance, but the will of the unseen that brought the book to this temple.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He carried the book to the chamber of dreamers beneath the temple, where pools and pillars formed from mineral and organic deposits. The blessed seawater flowed throughout as dreamers lay in small pools. He approached a dreamer, a female in her teenage years, whose hair undulated like living tendrils in the water beneath her. A clay jar by her head had the words "the book of dead names sees beyond the depths" etched into it. The Speaker gave the book to one of the dreamers' attendants and ordered that it be placed in an empty pool.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Speaker, do books dream?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It is the ocean that dreams. We are blessed to be a part of it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A voice from one of the pools spoke, "the dreams of the unseen permeate all creation." Everyone awake in the room chanted in response, "the dreams of the unseen permeate all creation."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And thus shall you be called," intoned the Speaker, his voice penetrating the sleep of the dreamer who spoke. He watched the attendant lay the book in the water. The attendant punctured a needle into the front cover, as he would into a vein, and lit the wick in the needle's tube. He did this out of habit; the book lacked the biology to carry the smoldering wax's substance throughout the bloodstream, but this was how the dreaming was induced.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It was two hours before any change was noted. The Speaker still stood over the dreamers, patient, faithful, and curious. The teenage girl stirred and minds melded in the stream. Her limbs twitched as the lingering consciousness from the book felt forgotten corporeality.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Speak," commanded the Speaker. The girl remained silent and made small splashes as she moved. The Speaker said, "I seek the source of whispers."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He continued his commands until the girl settled down. Finally she spoke in her young voice, "I refuse."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You are powerless to refuse. You will navigate the sea of dreams and find for me the source."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I can't move."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Tell me what you see."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I see everything. The dreams of everything. All at once, every one a shadow, fluid."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Look beyond them."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"There is only darkness beyond the dreams."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Go there. I compel you." His voice reverberated in the chamber. He had not chosen to pursue this. He didn't consider it a choice. He was following the will of his masters, as spoken through the dreamers.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Whispers... I feel them... Pressure... I can't understand them, but every syllable crushes me..."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Move toward it. I will speak to it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"There's a being-shapeless, immense... there's... an eye-"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At that moment the temple erupted with shrieks and wails of terror and pain. The Speaker fell forward and moaned, devoid of any thought or function. The young dreamer convulsed and died. At the temple's entrance worshippers ran into the town, possessed of nightmarish panic. They dashed themselves into walls and gouged at their throats with any tool available, trying to wake themselves from the nightmare they were in fact not in. Others remained in the temple, writhing and gurgling in the blessed water. Either they were stronger than the others, or perhaps more susceptible to the climactic vision, but they survived nonetheless. Of that moment, all could remember nothing more than the color yellow.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The temple was soon reopened for public worship. The surviving worshippers who rose to prominence joined the remaining priests. They became the caretakers of the temple that housed the Book of Sable, on whose pages appeared the names of the faithful who died for the Lord of Nightmares on that day.
chinese: 当夕阳沉入海洋，它的色彩层层叠加，铺洒在那片静谧的水面上。将熄的余晖以葡萄柚与血橙的色调穿透神殿的窗棂，与蓝与绿交融相映，却始终不曾相混。光影在小镇的屋顶上粼粼闪烁，如教堂钟声般辉映，信徒们纷纷走向海洋与神殿。对有些人而言，崇拜便是赞叹这海洋，亲临它的演出。另一些人则偏爱浸没其中，把身体交付给海水（这只是譬喻），以此来说一句「我把一切都归功于你」。神殿之内，虔信者沐浴在流动的海水里，任那乘着浓稠空气的熏香渗入肌肤。他们的心神随水流淌，让位给种种幻象与宁静。一位低语祭司在旁看守，殿堂的嘈杂中回荡着喃喃低语、哼吟，以及短促的狂喜之声。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]神殿更深处，「应急索具号」的灰眼船长向高阶代言者「其母之骨乃是明目」躬身行礼后，抬起了头。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你给我们带来了什么，船长？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]灰眼像任何一个成功的海船长该有的那样，对祭司们忠心耿耿。他常常祈祷，无论在浪上还是在岸上，也总把一份金色的战利品奉还给大海。正是这样的战利品，把他带到了家乡神殿里代言者的面前。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「卡拉比姆境内有传言说，为一件他们显然弄丢了的宝物开出了丰厚的赏金。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我知道。潮起潮落把天下各处的消息带给我。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「那你比我更清楚《赛博之书》的分量；我所知道的，不过是他们开出的价钱。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]代言者以一双不眨、深陷的眼睛凝视着。他无发、苍白、形容枯槁，可他的嗓音却像「应急索具号」桅杆的吱嘎作响。灰眼儿时在此礼拜时他便是代言者，如今相貌毫无改变。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你要什么价我都付。不过，讨价还价定妥之后，我有一事相求。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「您太慷慨了，共鸣尊者。若您以拉努恩钱币支付，我便按卡拉比姆开的价来。这桩相求我应下了——是什么事？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我要派一位女祭司随你的船同行。她有一项使命，你会发觉她的本事很有用处。把书留在祭坛上吧。你的效劳一如既往地无可替代，船长。」灰眼低头行礼，被人引了出去。代言者审视着面前的书。书封是浅色而单薄的皮革，肮脏而饱经风霜。书页正变得脆弱。无疑是人皮所制；这是书页地陵的产物，那里的书由魔像重重看守。从不曾有书离开过那座城，这使《赛博之书》格外稀有。高阶代言者明白，把这本书带到这座神殿的并非偶然，而是那不可见者的意志。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]他将书带往神殿之下的梦者之室，那里的水池与石柱由矿物与有机沉积物凝结而成。受祝福的海水贯流其间，梦者们躺卧在一个个小池中。他走近一名梦者，一个十来岁的少女，她的头发在身下的水中如活的卷须般起伏。她头旁有一只陶罐，罐上刻着一行字：「死名之书洞见于深渊之外」。代言者把书交给一名梦者的侍从，命他将书置于一个空池之中。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「代言者，书会做梦吗？」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「是海洋在做梦。我们有幸成为它的一部分。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]一个声音自某个水池中传来，「不可见者之梦浸透一切造物。」屋里所有清醒的人应声吟诵，「不可见者之梦浸透一切造物。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你便当以此为名，」代言者吟诵着，他的声音穿透了那开口梦者的睡眠。他看着侍从把书放入水中。侍从将一根针刺进书的前封，一如刺入血管，又点燃了针管里的灯芯。他这样做是出于习惯；这本书并无能把闷烧蜡质的成分输遍血流的生理构造，可梦境正是这样被诱发的。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]过了两个钟头才觉察到任何变化。代言者依旧立于梦者们之上，耐心、虔诚而好奇。那少女动了动，心神在水流中交融。她的四肢抽搐，那残留自书中的意识感到了久已遗忘的肉身之躯。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「说话，」代言者命道。少女沉默不语，只在移动时溅起小小的水花。代言者说：「我要寻找低语的源头。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]他不断下令，直到少女安定下来。她终于用稚嫩的嗓音开口：「我拒绝。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「你无力拒绝。你将航行于梦之海，替我找出那源头。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我动不了。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「告诉我你看见了什么。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「我看见一切。万物之梦。全都一齐涌来，每一个都是影，流动不定。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「望向它们之外。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「梦之外唯有黑暗。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「到那里去。我强令你。」他的声音在殿室中回荡。他并非自己选择追寻此事。他不认为这是一种选择。他遵从的是他那些主人的意志，一如梦者们所传达的。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「低语……我感觉到它们……那压力……我听不懂它们，可每一个音节都碾碎着我……」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「朝它去。我要与它对话。」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]「有一个存在——无形，庞大无边……那里……有一只眼——」[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]就在那一刻，神殿里骤然爆发出恐惧与痛楚的尖叫与哀嚎。代言者向前扑倒，呻吟着，失去了一切思想与知觉。那年轻的梦者抽搐着死去。神殿入口处，信徒们发着噩梦般的疯狂冲进镇中。他们把自己往墙上撞，用一切能抓到的工具剜割自己的喉咙，妄图从一场他们其实并不身处其中的噩梦里醒来。另一些人则留在神殿里，在受祝福的水中扭动、咯咯作响。要么是他们比旁人更强韧，要么或许是更易受那顶点幻象的侵袭，可无论如何，他们终究活了下来。至于那一刻，所有人所能记起的，不过是一种颜色——黄色。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]神殿不久便重新向公众开放礼拜。那些幸存下来、日后声名鹊起的信徒加入了余下的祭司之列。他们成了这座神殿的守护者，殿中藏着《赛博之书》，那一日为噩梦之主而死的虔信者之名，一一浮现于它的书页之上。

english: This world isn't big enough for the two of us! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 这个世界容不下我们两个！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: We have suffered your insolence for long enough! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 你的傲慢，我们已经受够了！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: Prepare to meet your doom! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 准备迎接你的末日吧！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: Now you shall pay for your many insults to the [OUR_EMPIRE]! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 现在，你要为对 [OUR_EMPIRE] 的种种侮辱付出代价！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: The time for talking is over, [CT_NAME]! We shall shall settle this on the field of battle! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 谈判到此为止，[CT_NAME]！让我们在战场上做个了断！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: Soon my numberless minions shall destroy you all! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 不久，我数之不尽的爪牙将把你们统统毁灭！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）
是时候受死了，[CT_NAME]。（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: Fool! Now we shall destroy you! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 蠢货！现在我们要将你毁灭！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: I suppose you realize, this means war. ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 我想你也明白，这意味着战争。（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: Mighty [OUR_EMPIRE] has had enough of your treachery and deceit! Now you must pay! ([OUR_NAME] declares war!)
chinese: 强大的 [OUR_EMPIRE] 已受够了你的背叛与欺诈！现在你必须付出代价！（[OUR_NAME] 宣战！）

english: Greetings! I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_EMPIRE]. I hope that our two great peoples can live together in peace.
chinese: 您好！我是 [OUR_EMPIRE] 的 [OUR_NAME]。我希望我们两个伟大的民族能够和平共处。

english: Welcome, [CT_NAME]! I cannot tell a lie: I'm darned glad to meet you!
chinese: 欢迎，[CT_NAME]！我不会说谎：见到你我真是高兴得不得了！

english: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! It is an honor to meet you! May the heavens bestow upon you an empire only slightly less glorious than mine!
chinese: 您好，[CT_NAME]！能与你相见真是荣幸！愿上苍赐予你一个帝国——只比我的稍逊一筹便好！

english: I am pleased to meet you, [CT_NAME]! Let us each slaughter fifty thousand slaves to celebrate this auspicious occasion.
chinese: 很高兴见到你，[CT_NAME]！让我们各自宰杀五万名奴隶，来庆祝这个吉祥的时刻吧。

english: Greetings, honorable [CT_NAME]. Let us hope that there will always be peace and friendship between [OUR_EMPIRE] and [CT_CIV_SHORT] - for that is all that stands between you and immediate annihilation.
chinese: 您好，尊敬的 [CT_NAME]。但愿 [OUR_EMPIRE] 与 [CT_CIV_SHORT] 之间永享和平与友谊——因为唯有它，才隔在你与顷刻的灭亡之间。

english: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. It is a pleasure to meet you. Here: have a copy of my little red book. You might learn something.
chinese: 您好，[CT_NAME]。很高兴见到你。喏：拿一本我的红宝书吧。你或许能从中学到些东西。

english: Surely the gods have smiled upon you, [CT_NAME] - for they have led you to me!
chinese: 诸神必定是在向你微笑，[CT_NAME]——因为他们把你引到了我的面前！

english: Welcome to my palace, [CT_NAME]. I'm [OUR_NAME], the wise and really quite beautiful leader of mighty [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Let there be peace between us or we'll kill you.
chinese: 欢迎来到我的宫殿，[CT_NAME]。我是 [OUR_NAME]，强大的 [OUR_CIV_SHORT] 那位睿智而又相当美丽的君主。愿我们之间和平相处，否则我们就杀了你。

english: Good day to you, [CT_NAME]. We are [OUR_NAME], ruler of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Please do not hesitate to call upon us if you need assistance - God commands us give aid and comfort to our inferiors...
chinese: 日安，[CT_NAME]。朕乃 [OUR_NAME]，[OUR_CIV_SHORT] 之君。若你需要援助，尽管来求我们——上帝令我们向卑下者施以援手与慰藉……

english: Welcome! I am [OUR_NAME], absolute monarch of mighty [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and indisputably the handsomest and best-dressed ruler in the entire history of the universe. Wouldn't you agree?
chinese: 欢迎！我是 [OUR_NAME]，强大的 [OUR_CIV_SHORT] 之绝对君主，也无可争辩地是宇宙有史以来最英俊、最会穿着的统治者。你不同意吗？

english: Greetings. I'm [OUR_NAME], Emperor, Marshal, and First Citizen of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. You can call me "Little Corporal," but then I'll have to kill you.
chinese: 您好。我是 [OUR_NAME]，[OUR_CIV_SHORT] 的皇帝、元帅兼第一公民。你可以叫我"小伍长"，不过那样我就得杀了你。

english: [OUR_CIV_SHORT] the great and its superior people greet you. I, [OUR_NAME], desire peace with all my neighbors - even with your puny culture.
chinese: 伟大的 [OUR_CIV_SHORT] 及其优越的人民向你致意。我，[OUR_NAME]，愿与所有邻邦和平相处——哪怕是你那点微不足道的文化。

english: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! I am [OUR_NAME], ruler of the warlike [OUR_EMPIRE]! Let us join together and crush the world's armies beneath our sandals! It'll be way cool!
chinese: 您好，[CT_NAME]！我是 [OUR_NAME]，好战的 [OUR_EMPIRE] 之统治者！让我们联手，把天下的军队踩在我们的凉鞋之下！那可太酷了！

english: The [OUR_EMPIRE] welcomes the glorious [CT_CIV_ADJ] people and their leader, [CT_NAME]. You play ceremonial ball with us, we'll play ceremonial ball with you.
chinese: [OUR_EMPIRE] 欢迎光荣的 [CT_CIV_ADJ] 人民及其领袖 [CT_NAME]。你和我们玩祭祀球赛，我们也和你玩祭祀球赛。

english: May peace and happiness go with you always, [CT_NAME]. I am [OUR_NAME] of [OUR_CIV_SHORT].
chinese: 愿和平与幸福永远伴你左右，[CT_NAME]。我是 [OUR_CIV_SHORT] 的 [OUR_NAME]。

english: Welcome to my humble home, [CT_NAME]. [OUR_CIV_SHORT] desires peace with all of her neighbors - even the really annoying ones like yours.
chinese: 欢迎来到我简陋的家，[CT_NAME]。[OUR_CIV_SHORT] 愿与所有邻邦和平相处——哪怕是像你这样十分讨厌的邻居。

english: Welcome, [CT_NAME]! May your empire flourish and grow for as long as it remains useful to us! I mean that sincerely.
chinese: 欢迎，[CT_NAME]！愿你的帝国繁荣壮大，只要它对我们还有用处！我这话是真心的。

english: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. I, [OUR_NAME], humble ruler of [OUR_CIV_SHORT], offer my hand to you in friendship.
chinese: 欢迎，[CT_NAME]。我，[OUR_NAME]，[OUR_CIV_SHORT] 谦卑的统治者，向你伸出友谊之手。

english: Welcome, oh leader of the [CT_EMPIRE]. My horde can beat your horde any day of the week. Shall we be friends or enemies?
chinese: 欢迎，[CT_EMPIRE] 的领袖啊。我的部众任何时候都能击败你的部众。我们是做朋友，还是做敌人？

english: The mighty [OUR_EMPIRE] greets you. Let us work together to achieve the total destruction of our foes, and only THEN betray and rend each other like the rabid dogs we truly are!
chinese: 强大的 [OUR_EMPIRE] 向你致意。让我们携手实现对敌人的彻底毁灭，然后——也唯有到那时——再像我们本性中那群疯狗一样彼此背叛、彼此撕咬！

english: Greetings, oh wise ruler of the [CT_CIV_ADJ] peoples! [OUR_CIV_SHORT] is strong - shall we count you among our friends, or among our enemies?
chinese: 您好，[CT_CIV_ADJ] 人民睿智的统治者啊！[OUR_CIV_SHORT] 很强大——我们该把你算作朋友，还是算作敌人？

english: Welcome to [OUR_CIV_SHORT], [CT_NAME]. Care for some salad? I made it myself.
chinese: 欢迎来到 [OUR_CIV_SHORT]，[CT_NAME]。来点沙拉吗？我亲手做的。
